To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the seasonal patterns of methyl mercury and essential fatty acids (EFAs) concentrations in planktonic foodwebs are different and that the cladocerans bioaccumulate methyl mercury, but do not convey as much of the essential fatty acid, docosahexanoic acid (DHa), as copepods do.
methyl mercury bioaccumulates in the food web with increasing size, whereas the essential fatty acids (EFAs) do not.

methyl mercury concentrations in planktonic organisms increased with increasing zooplancton size and were independent on plankton taxonomy, while essential fatty acids increased from sestonic to copepod-dominated mesozooplanks, but decreased in cladoceran-dominanted macrozooplanktons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether the structure of planktivorous food webs can affect dietary exposure to essential nutrients and potentially toxic compounds.
the seasonal variability of MeHg and EFA concentrations in the planktic food web.
a fundamental question: how do essential nutrients and toxic substances interact in food webs?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EFA and MeHg concentrations vary seasonally, but that the seasonal variation in EFA and MeHG concentrations are not related to each other.
EFA and MeHg are essential dietary substances, but that MeHg is a potentially toxic one.

planktonic food chain length and structure, as well as plankton taxonomy, are important factors regulating the transfer and availability of essential nutrients, and that the bioavailability of toxic substances is independent of these factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the seasonal dynamics of MeHg and EFA in planktonic food chains is strongly influenced by the seasonal succession and size structure of plankton communities, which in turn affect the trophic transfer of MeHg to fish.
the seasonal variability of EFA and MeHg in the plankton is driven by seasonal changes in planktonic food chain structure and the resulting differences in the EFA content of the plankton.

the seasonal variation in the plankton community structure and its effect on the bioaccumulation of MeHg is a critical factor in the transfer of MeHg to top predators, and that this transfer is independent of plankton taxonomic structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MeHg and EFA are not always co-occurring in plankton, and that the structure of planktic food webs can influence the dietary intake of EFA and MeHg.
planktonic food chains, in addition to their role as a source of toxic contaminants to higher consumers, also regulate access of fish and other higher consumers to essential fatty acids.
MeHg and EFA are both important dietary components, but their concentrations and patterns in plankton are different.
